sourceAttempts.result: The City describes the Albuquerque Rio Grande as generally calm with no technical rapids, identifies legal non-motorized boating, names Calabacillas, Central Avenue and Rio Bravo access, and gives a roughly 400–500 cfs feasible-paddling reference for the broader corridor.
The City identifies the public park facilities, sunrise-to-sunset access, bosque setting and Rio Bravo Riverside Picnic Area; overnight riverbank camping is not assumed.

sourceAttempts.family: Quiet Waters access and outing review
sourceAttempts.result: Quiet Waters publishes water-entry coordinate references, carry and diversion cautions, and distinct RGVSP North, South and Full Run itineraries.
USGS 08329918 at Alameda Bridge is a direct Rio Grande discharge and stage station with current telemetry and a long record; it is used as the upstream corridor reference.
The existing Rio Grande New Mexico Commons photograph is retained as same-river context and is attributed to the Bureau of Land Management via Wikimedia Commons.

thresholdEvidence.reachApplicability: City guidance says roughly 400–500 cfs generally provides feasible paddling conditions from the north Rio Grande Valley State Park corridor toward the southern boundary; low and high flows, wind, cold water and channel conditions still require an on-site decision.

validation: Focused Albuquerque Rio Grande route safety test passed.
